overview: Albert of Mecklenburg was German duke elected king of Sweden, later defeated by Margaret I in the struggle for Scandinavian power. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1364 — Becomes king of Sweden; 1389 — Defeated at Åsle and captured.
He died in 1412, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Albert of Mecklenburg was German duke elected king of Sweden, later defeated by Margaret I in the struggle for Scandinavian power. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1364 — Becomes king of Sweden; 1389 — Defeated at Åsle and captured.
He died in 1412, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Albert of Mecklenburg was born c. 1338. His family background is usually placed in House of Mecklenburg, though early Scandinavian genealogy can be uncertain and politically shaped.

Albert of Mecklenburg's early life belonged to the medieval Scandinavian world, where kinship, sea routes, church contacts, assemblies, and armed followings shaped the opportunities available to a ruler.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Albert of Mecklenburg, a German prince raised to the Swedish throne by nobles seeking a pliable king, is remembered as a foreign ruler who failed to win the loyalty of his adopted realm. The sources present a monarch dependent on German favourites and resented by the Swedish aristocracy that had invited him, whose attempts to assert royal authority alienated the very magnates who had made him king.

His reign collapsed in conflict with the powerful councillors and ultimately with Margaret I of Denmark, who defeated and captured him at the Battle of Falköping in 1389. A famous gibe attributed to the episode — mockery involving a whetstone and a long fool's cap — fixed his humiliation in tradition.

The hostile Swedish memory, shaped by those who rejected him, presents a weak and unpopular foreign king out of step with his kingdom. He is remembered chiefly for his failure and capture rather than for any positive quality, a cautionary figure of misjudged foreign kingship.

contentSections.title: As king of Sweden
paragraphs: Albert was brought to power by Swedish opponents of Magnus Eriksson. His reign depended on aristocratic support and German connections, but opposition grew over land and power.

As King of Sweden, Duke of Mecklenburg, Albert of Mecklenburg had to turn dynastic claim into workable authority through alliances, military pressure, church support, and acceptance by regional elites.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Died in Mecklenburg in 1412 after losing the Swedish crown to the forces supporting Margaret I.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: He is remembered chiefly as the rival Margaret I defeated on the path to the Kalmar Union.
Later saga, saintly, or national traditions often amplified Albert of Mecklenburg's reputation, so the article separates near-contemporary evidence from later memory where possible.

timeline.title: Born
timeline.description: Albert of Mecklenburg was born around c. 1338, but the birthplace is not securely recorded. The date is approximate, but it places the early life in the setting of Kingdom of Sweden.

timeline.title: Becomes king of Sweden
timeline.description: Albert became king with support from Swedish nobles opposed to Magnus Eriksson, bringing Mecklenburg interests into Swedish politics.

timeline.title: Defeated at Åsle and captured
timeline.description: Albert was defeated and captured by Margaret I at Åsle in 1389, opening the way for her control over Sweden.

timeline.title: Death
timeline.description: Died in Mecklenburg in 1412 after losing the Swedish crown to the forces supporting Margaret I.

timeline.title: Aftermath and memory
timeline.description: Albert’s defeat allowed Margaret I to dominate Sweden and helped shift Scandinavian politics toward the Kalmar Union.
